_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)

pivotal_trials.population: Adults with histologically confirmed, locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC, ECOG PS 0 or 1, measurable disease per RECIST v1.1; both ROS1 TKI-naive and one prior ROS1 TKI
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review (BICR)
pivotal_trials.n: TRUST-I: 103 TKI-naive and 66 TKI-pretreated NSCLC patients
pivotal_trials.result: TKI-naive (n=103): ORR 90% (95% CI 83, 95), median DOR not reached (95% CI 30.4, NR). TKI-pretreated (n=66): ORR 52% (95% CI 39, 64), median DOR 13.2 months (95% CI 7.7, 24.9)

pivotal_trials.population: Adults with histologically confirmed, locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC, ECOG PS 0 or 1, measurable disease per RECIST v1.1; both ROS1 TKI-naive and one prior ROS1 TKI
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review (BICR)
pivotal_trials.n: TRUST-II: 54 TKI-naive and 47 TKI-pretreated NSCLC patients
pivotal_trials.result: TKI-naive (n=54): ORR 85% (95% CI 73, 93). TKI-pretreated (n=47): ORR 62% (95% CI 46, 75)

key_safety: Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions: diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, rash, constipation, fatigue. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 31% of patients (pneumonia 7%, pleural effusion 4.7%, hepatotoxicity 2.4%); fatal adverse reactions in 18 (5%) patients. Warnings include hepatotoxicity (AST increased in 88%, ALT increased in 85%), ILD/pneumonitis, and QTc prolongation
target_moa: CNS-penetrant tyrosine kinase inhibitor of ROS1 (including resistance mutations G2032R, L1951R, L2026M, D2033N) with activity against TRK A/B/C; inhibits growth of cancer cells expressing ROS1 fusion genes and mutations
companion_dx_detail: Patients are selected based on ROS1 rearrangement(s) in tumor specimens, but no FDA-approved test for ROS1 rearrangement selection is currently available; local labs used NGS, PCR, FISH, or IHC

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee, as no significant efficacy or safety issues required external input

basis.text: The application received Priority review designation

summary.text: IBTROZI received traditional (full) approval under a Priority review; it had been granted Breakthrough therapy designation (2022) and Orphan drug designation (2024). Approval was based on ORR and DOR from two single-arm studies (TRUST-I and TRUST-II) without accelerated approval.

citations.quote: The data submitted by the Applicant provide substantial evidence of effectiveness to support the traditional approval of taletrectinib for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic *ROS1*-positive NSCLC.

Breakthrough therapy designation was granted on 01 Aug 2022 for the treatment of adult patients with advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC who are ROS1 TKI treatment naïve or previously treated with crizotinib.

Orphan drug designation was granted on 16 Jul 2024 for the treatment of ROS1-positive, NTRK-positive, anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive, leukocyte receptor tyrosine kinase receptor-positive, activated Cdc42-associated kinase-positive, or discoidin domain receptor 1-positive NSCLC.

The recommendation for traditional approval is based on the results from two single-arm studies in patients with advanced *ROS1*-positive NSCLC and other solid tumors: Study AB-106-G208 (Study G208 or TRUST-II, NCT04919811) and Study AB-106-C203 (Study C203 or TRUST-I, NCT04395677).
